clue.text: Backchat and criticism for a cosmetic

parts.note: lip is cheeky talk, insolent backchat
to get stick is to receive harsh criticism

explanation.surface: Someone cheeky earns a telling-off over their make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A coloured stick of wax applied to the lips is a familiar item of make-up.

clue.text: Quietly enraged buccaneer

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for playing quietly
irate means furious, enraged

explanation.surface: A seafaring robber seething in silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Buccaneers were sea robbers of the Caribbean, a kind of seafaring outlaw.

clue.text: Man going into Conservative hypothesis

indicators.note: one piece enters another, so the word for man sits inside the party word

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
he stands for a man, the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man joins the Tory party with an idea he wants to test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person entering politics, but it is only the pronoun; 'going into' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a proposed explanation, a hypothesis awaiting proof.

clue.text: Raucous ego running riot, not deterred by danger

indicators.note: things running riot are out of control and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A loud, unruly self-importance gone wild, fearless in the face of peril.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running riot' rearranges the ten letters of RAUCOUS EGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone brave is not put off by peril; that is the plain sense of fearless boldness.

clue.text: Trousers, with top trimmed, might contain these

definitions.text: Trousers, with top trimmed, might contain these

indicators.note: the top of a word written across is its first letter, here cut off

parts.note: pants is a word for trousers, especially in American English

explanation.surface: A warning that insects may be lurking in your trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: PANTS loses its first letter. The whole clue also defines: 'ants in your pants' describes restless fidgeting, as if insects were inside your trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Small insects may crawl inside clothing; the idiom about restlessness pictures exactly that.

clue.text: Many hesitant words interrupting common sense

indicators.note: the hesitations break into the middle of the word for common sense

parts.note: nous is practical intelligence, common sense
um and er are the two sounds of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A speaker keeps stammering through an otherwise sensible argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupting' signals that the hesitation sounds break into the word for common sense; 'common' is part of that phrase, not a separate clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Numerous means great in number, which is the sense of many.

clue.text: Use up about a pound on birds now and then — very impressive

indicators.note: the spending word goes around the pound symbol, enclosing it

parts.note: to spend is to use up or consume
L, from the Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

indicators.note: taking letters only occasionally, so every other letter of the word is kept

explanation.surface: Someone splashes out on birds every so often and the result is grand.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside SPEND to give SPLEND; 'now and then' takes the 2nd and 4th letters of 'birds', I and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendid describes something magnificent, which is to say very impressive.

clue.text: A slight obsession about New York, nothing specific

indicators.note: the article and the obsession word wrap around the city abbreviation

parts.note: to have a thing about something is to be mildly obsessed with it

explanation.surface: A mild fixation with New York that doesn't amount to much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' has the article and the obsession word wrap around the city; to have 'a thing about' something is an idiom for a mild fixation.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'any old item will do' means no particular one is required: nothing specific.

clue.text: Cube cooked in empty grill

indicators.note: the cooked letters are placed inside the word for empty

parts.note: bare means empty, with nothing in it

indicators.note: cooked here means altered or prepared, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cube of meat is cooked on a grill with nothing else on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges the letters of 'Cube'; 'in' puts them inside the word for empty. 'grill' looks like wordplay but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor cooking rack over coals is used to grill food, so it serves as a grill.

clue.text: Runs away from skirmish in the wild

indicators.note: the runs abbreviation is taken out of the skirmish word

parts.note: a brush is a brief encounter or skirmish, as in a brush with the enemy
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Fleeing from a fight out in the wilderness.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia and Africa the uncultivated back country is called this; it is untamed wild land.

clue.text: Utilise printer's measurement stratagem

parts.note: an em is a unit of measurement in printing, the width of the letter M
a ploy is a cunning tactic, a stratagem

explanation.surface: Making use of a typesetter's trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something to use is to utilise it, as when one makes use of a tool.

clue.text: Organisation of Easter Sunday not seen, sadly, on this earlier day

indicators.note: organising letters puts them into a new arrangement, signalling an anagram
signals that some letters are left out of the pool being rearranged
a second hint at disorder, the letters ending up in a sorry state

explanation.surface: Easter Sunday is mourned in advance on the day before it.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the letters S, E, E, N from EASTER SUNDAY and rearrange the remaining eight. 'sadly' also fits Holy Saturday, a day of mourning before Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: The day preceding Easter Sunday is the last day of the week, the earlier day referred to.

clue.text: Offshoot of British stock farm

parts.note: a ranch is a large farm raising livestock

explanation.surface: A spin-off of a British livestock farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb growing from a tree trunk, or a subsidiary office, is an offshoot.

clue.text: Group offering

definitions.meaning: an assembled set of items, as in a stamp hoard
the money gathered from a church congregation during a service

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an assembled set and money gathered at a church service.

clue.text: Determination concerning explanation

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
a solution is an answer or explanation to a problem

explanation.surface: A firm resolve about finding an answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolve or firmness of purpose is the sense of determination meant here.

clue.text: Testimony of English study in immorality

indicators.note: the study word goes inside the immorality word

parts.note: vice is wicked or immoral behaviour
a den is a private room for work, a study

explanation.surface: An English academic investigating wickedness gives a statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' reads as a verb about research, but it is a noun for a private room; 'in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Testimony given in court is proof offered to support a case.

clue.text: Clueless, I admit, about two major components of air

indicators.note: the word for admit goes around the two chemical symbols

parts.note: to grant a point is to admit or concede it
nitrogen and oxygen, chemical symbols N and O, make up most of the air

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to knowing nothing about what air is made of.
explanation.walkthrough: N and O go inside GRANT after its G.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking knowledge or awareness is to be without a clue, uninformed.

clue.text: Press caught youngster resistant to change

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a lad is a boy, a youngster

explanation.surface: Reporters catch a young person who won't budge.
explanation.definitionFit: Something armoured with metal plates is rigid and fixed, like an unbreakable agreement.

clue.text: Virology crudely interrupted by America using force?

indicators.note: the America abbreviation breaks into the rearranged letters
done roughly or crudely, the letters are put in a rough new order

parts.note: US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: American science is accused of forcing its way into the study of viruses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crudely' rearranges the letters of 'Virology', and 'interrupted by' breaks them to let America's abbreviation in, giving VIGORO + US + LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with energy and strength means acting forcefully; the question mark admits the loose equivalence.

clue.text: Outside each day, cut field

indicators.note: the cut word goes outside the abbreviations, enclosing them

parts.note: to mow grass is to cut it

explanation.surface: Every day out of doors, the grass is cut in the paddock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' looks like 'outdoors' in the surface, but it tells the cut word to wrap around the abbreviations for each and day.
explanation.definitionFit: A grassy field used for hay or grazing is the meaning here.

clue.text: Sinew of edible shellfish we're told

indicators.note: what is told is spoken, so the shellfish word is heard rather than written

parts.note: a mussel is an edible bivalve shellfish

explanation.surface: The stringy tissue of a seafood dish, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew suggests physical strength and the body's working tissue, as in brawn.

clue.text: Schemes of identification for low islands

definitions.meaning: the legends on a map or chart that explain its symbols
low coral islets, as off the coast of Florida

explanation.definitionFit: Map legends identify symbols, and Florida's chain of low coral islets bears the same name.

clue.text: Submerges in river in undulating pasture-land

indicators.note: the river abbreviation is placed in the middle of the pasture word

parts.note: the downs are rolling grassy chalk hills in southern England

explanation.surface: Someone plunges into a stream running through hilly grassland.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside DOWNS after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: To push something under water so it is covered is to submerge or flood it.

clue.text: Tortuous clue she'd programme

indicators.note: tortuous means twisting, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A crossword solver complains about a twisty clue a woman has set.
explanation.definitionFit: A timetable or plan of events is a programme.

clue.text: In an orderly way, almost, with time for beginning of romance

indicators.note: one letter takes the place of another, the time letter standing in for the other

parts.note: nearly means almost

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A tidy romance that almost happened, if the timing had been right.
explanation.walkthrough: NEARLY swaps its R (the first letter of 'romance') for T.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things tidily, with everything in its place, is acting in an orderly way.

clue.text: Structures carrying transport through channels

parts.note: via means by way of, through
ducts are tubes or channels for carrying fluid or air

explanation.surface: Bridges carrying traffic along water channels.
explanation.definitionFit: Long arched bridges carry a road or railway across a valley.

clue.text: Trend restricted, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the word for restricted is taken by its sound

parts.note: tied means bound or restricted

explanation.surface: A fashion that is apparently limited.
explanation.definitionFit: The general drift of opinion is a current, as in the turning of public opinion.

clue.text: In no particular place when year changes

indicators.note: letters that change are rearranged into a different order

explanation.surface: Somewhere vague at New Year.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb meaning in any location at all, no specific spot.
